text:
alex (Support): FYI I just got a customer escalation from Acme. They started seeing bursts of 429s and a bunch of requests routed to us-west even though their account region is eu-central. Ticket #12345. Pasting their log snippet below and tagging eng oncall.

acme_ops (Acme Inc.): This started 2026-03-15T08:12Z. ~2k req/s burst. Many requests failing 429 then the next attempt goes to us-west and latency jumps to 700-1200ms. Product degraded.

alex (Support): Can you share how you're calling the API? host used, headers, and a minimal curl so we can repro. Also include any auth token id.

acme_ops (Acme Inc.): We call https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate with header `X-Preferred-Region: eu-central` and our token `tkn_XXXX`. We expect eu only. Example log lines: `route_decision: eu-central -> queue(overflow) -> fallback: nearest` and `x-upstream: us-west-1`

maria (ENG-oncall): Thanks — checking routing logs for account acme. I can see repeated `capacity_exhausted` events for eu-central at 08:12:03-08:12:45. Route decision: preferred=eu-central, policy=allow_cross_region_fallback, chosen=us-west-1. That matches their symptom.

jia (Platform): Confirmed — our fallback policy for that account was set to `prefer_latency` (which allows cross-region routing to any pool with capacity). Two immediate options: (1) change fallback to `region-only` (will keep traffic in eu and cause queueing/429s when saturated) or (2) add temporary burst/dedicated capacity in eu.

sam (Networking): Also noting the token in their logs was issued with `scope: global` earlier this week, so token-level routing allowed non-eu endpoints. If you want strict region isolation we should reissue a region-restricted token.

alex (Support): Customer asks for a short-term mitigation that avoids cross-region latency. Which of the two options is quickest?

maria (ENG-oncall): Quickest is to bump their account queue and enable the burst pool for 24h, and simultaneously flip fallback to `region-only` so requests don't spill to us-west. I'll perform the changes now. Commands I will run:

```
# temp account changes (admin only)
POST /admin/accounts/acme/config 
body: {"queue_depth":200, "fallback_mode":"region-only", "enable_burst":true} 
```

jia (Platform): If you prefer CLI: `rb-cli accounts update acme --queue-depth 200 --fallback region-only --enable-burst`

sam (Networking): I'll also issue a new token scoped to eu only: new token id `tkn_7f3a9e`. Client must rotate it immediately; I'll DM this securely.

kevin (Billing): Quick billing note: enabling burst/dedicated capacity will increase charges. Estimated delta at current load ~ +$2.4k/day. Need customer ack before we leave it on long-term.

acme_ops (Acme Inc.): We authorize a 24h burst. Please proceed. Also reissue the token now and I'll rotate.

maria (ENG-oncall): Actions applied: `set_account_config acme {queue_depth:200, fallback:region-only, enable_burst:true}` -> success. Monitoring live.

observability-bot: [metric link] acme.request.rps eu-central: spike -> 2.1k at 08:12 UTC. eu-central 429-rate fell from 18% -> 6% within 3m after config change. cross-region calls dropped ~95%.

sam (Networking): New token issued and DM'd. Note: original token had global scope; rotating to `scope: region:eu-central` prevents routing outside eu.

acme_ops (Acme Inc.): Confirming rotation done. Seeing median latency back to ~80-120ms and very few 429s now. Will monitor for the next 24h. Thanks. :thumbsup:

alex (Support): Great — I'll keep the ticket open until tomorrow when you confirm no regression. I'll also capture repro steps and the exact config changes in the ticket notes for handoff to account management.

maria (ENG-oncall): Follow-up: We'll create a short runbook item for accounts with bursty traffic to pre-authorize temporary capacity and region-lock fallback. Filing a follow-up task in eng-platform.

acme_ops (Acme Inc.): Appreciate the quick turnaround. Keep me posted if any further billable changes happen.

alex (Support): Noted. Closing loop once 24h check is complete.
